en: Thomas Boston put it this way:

text:
사람이 문제 많은
이웃을 만나면 *이사* 가면 되죠
en: "A troublesome neighbor? You can move.

text:
아주 힘든 직장 상사를 만나면
*직장*을 옮기면 됩니다
en: A terrible boss? You can change jobs.

text:
어려운 가족이 있으면
안 만나면 되고
en: A difficult family? Stop seeing them,
or leave home.
But whether a believer goes to the wilderness,
pitches a tent on a rocky island,

text:
짐승이나 새들이 없는
바다의 저 먼 곳에 가든
en: or goes far out to sea, past every beast and bird,

text:
인간의 *부패한 마음*은
그와 함께 할 것이다
en: his corrupt heart will go with him.

text:
그 본성은 *그림자*가
몸을 따르듯이 그를 따라갈
en: It will follow him like a shadow follows a body."
This wretched human nature —
we need to fear it.
The gospel opens our eyes to it.
We have a fallen nature.
Without grace we always fall —
we need to live with that fear.

text:
경건한 신자는
부패한 옛 본성을 대항합니다
en: The godly believer fights their old corrupt nature.
They strain every nerve to kill it.
So what they work and work at
is holy habits.

text:
인생이 무너지지 않으려면
거룩한 습관을 잡아야 돼
en: If you don't want your life to fall apart, build holy habits.

text:
거룩한 습관이 없는 사람은
삶이 힘들면 *무너집니다*
en: Without them, when life gets hard, you fall apart.
Even falling apart, you wake up and go jogging:
that's the routine you need.

text:
그렇지 않으면 우리의
본성을 이길 수가 없어요
en: Otherwise we can't beat our nature.
